series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #17 (the big session)
hook: Practising for two hours every Sunday is the slowest way to learn anything.

gate.goal_link: any skill goal (piano, code, a language) moves faster with the same weekly time
gate.mechanism: spacing: skills consolidate between sessions (much of it during sleep), so 7 short sessions beat 1 long one; plus one busy Sunday zeroes the week
gate.universal: 'I'll practise at the weekend' is how most adults schedule a skill

frame.want: learn a skill with the time you have
frame.obstacle: one weekly block: forgotten by next week, and skipped whenever Sunday gets busy
frame.cost: a missed Sunday = 0 minutes that week vs 120 when one of seven 20-min days is missed (real arithmetic)
frame.fix: same 140 minutes, 20 a day, anchored to dinner / before work / commute

hooks_considered.line: Practising for two hours every Sunday is the slowest way to learn anything.
